why: SCC-417 revert-proof. Code-derived: each mutant flips ONE decision in the two widened _BANNED_PATTERNS entries and must die by the case that pins that decision alone. M1 = NARROW the your-call entry back to the forward order (the SCC-416 defect, half of it). M2 = NARROW it back to the singular (the other half). M3 = DELETE the cross-repo entry (the shape no entry knew). M4 = WIDEN the cross-repo entry by dropping the scoped case-sensitivity, so 'its own two tickets' matches. M5 = WIDEN the reversed arm's window from 40 to 400 characters, so an honest landing-order row 85 characters wide matches. M1-M3 are killed by the B11 single-shape pins; M4 and M5 by the B12 near-miss pins - a widening that no near-miss can see is a widening nobody measured. Review additions, each REPRODUCED by an in-memory mutant before it was declared: M6 (R1) = NARROW the another-board's entry back to a bare key, so 'its own `AVCH` tickets' slips through again - killed by the B11 backtick pin. M7 (R2) = NARROW the reversed arm to the singular only; under M2 both arms lose the plural and the forward plural row kills it, but the reversed-plural SCC-416 row is ALSO caught by the another-board's entry, so M7 survived every case until the reversed-plural B11 row existed. M8 (R3) = WIDEN the FORWARD arm's window 40 -> 400; M5 pins only the reversed arm, and the plan promised a near-miss on each side - killed by B12.7 (a forward pair 107 characters apart). M9 (R4) = drop `their` - killed by the plural-owner pin. M10 = NARROW the another-board's entry to the plural only - killed by the bold singular pin (the only other singular row, create/mint, is entry 0's).
